# Primary review for the 7 September reference renewal

This review was performed in the existing implementation maintenance context. It
is primary review, not a blinded independent challenge. The preserved original
audit and workbench retain all preceding judgments, annotations, dates, responses,
and reconciliation artifacts. No new checker or calibration identity is invented.

The primary reviewer reread every source line, both normalized obligations, every
atomic annotation, the ledger support moves, issue I-001, registry use D001, the
eight cross-unit checks, and the method-interface scope. The manuscript contains
no external theorem application or numerical implementation claim requiring an
additional interface. Existing calibration provenance remains historical and is
retained only if the current software accepts it for the same configuration.

For the lemma, fixing an arbitrary positive tolerance on line 14 and unfolding
fixed-index convergence on line 15 are valid. The passage to a maximum over a
growing set on line 16 is invalid. On a countable product probability space take
independent Bernoulli random variables with success probability $1/n$ and $m_n=n^2$.
For every fixed index and every $0<\varepsilon<1$ the tail is $1/n$, and it is zero for
$\varepsilon\geq1$. Every hypothesis therefore holds. At $\varepsilon=1/2$,

$$
P\!\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq n^2}|X_{n,j}|>\frac12\right)
=1-(1-1/n)^{n^2}\longrightarrow1,
\qquad (1-1/n)^{n^2}\leq e^{-n}.
$$

Folding the
definition on line 17 cannot establish the conclusion, and this same witness
directly refutes the exact lemma conclusion. The finite rational computations
illustrate the identity; the exponential bound supplies the asymptotic argument.

A uniform tail rate with $m_n a_n(\varepsilon)\to0$ is a sufficient candidate repair,
not a necessary condition for every possible array. The renewed annotation makes
that distinction explicit. The current hypothesis does not supply control of
the growing union by any route. A fixed finite index range is another meaningful
candidate, with a narrower claim. Neither proposal is recorded as an implemented
repair, and issue I-001 remains open.

For the theorem, the statement reference inherits the lemma's hypotheses, while
the proof reference requests the lemma conclusion through D001. The requested
form, probability measure, quantifiers, growing range, and regime match exactly.
The equality $\hat\theta_n-\theta_0=\max_j |X_{n,j}|$ is an exact substitution, so the
local algebra is valid conditional on the unavailable imported premise. The
complete written argument remains invalid under the existing judgment contract.
Separately, on a one-point probability space choose $m_n=n$ and $X_{n,j}=\mathbf{1}\{j=n\}$.
Every fixed coordinate is zero for all $n>j$, every row maximum equals one, and the
estimator error equals one for every $n$. Its probability of exceeding $1/2$ is
therefore always one. This directly refutes the exact theorem statement without
inferring downstream falsity solely from a failed supporting proof.

Both C001 statements remain refuted and both complete written arguments remain
invalid. The lemma has no external dependency defect; the theorem's dependency
closure is incorrect because D001 cannot supply its premise. The application
form matches, but effective use-site sufficiency is insufficient. All normalized
conditions and issue targets remain unchanged. Refreshed primary packets bind
the current protocol and conservative source context. The theorem packet is
prepared after the renewed lemma ledger so any dependency evidence identity is
current. Old independent checks remain intact until genuine new responses are
recorded, allowing the normal supersession chain to preserve prior reviews.

The first-time compiler CLI requires an absent ledger, which conflicts with the
live issue origin during renewal. The preparation script therefore uses fresh
extracted skeletons and the existing compiler library, validates each complete
candidate locally, preserves the old ledger in history, and only then replaces
the working-copy primary record. It does not change source, falsify independent
review, or publish the reference. Exact current challenge packets go to separate
fresh contexts only after this primary preparation is complete.
